music.brief: Low steady pulse under a soft string pad, calm and focused, one gentle lift near the end, instrumental, for a short explainer video, about 60 seconds.

sources: DeLoache et al. (2010). Do babies learn from baby media? Psychological Science.
Robb et al. (2009). Just a talking book? British Journal of Developmental Psychology.
Strouse et al. (2021). Learning from video: A meta-analysis of the video deficit in children ages 0 to 6 years. Child Development.

beats.text: Baby word videos taught no extra words.
beats.say: Baby word videos taught no extra words.

beats.text: Stay for three everyday moments to teach words tonight.
beats.say: Stay for three everyday moments to teach words tonight.

beats.text: Babies 12 to 18 months watched a popular word DVD for 4 weeks.
beats.sub: They learned no more words than babies who never saw it.
beats.say: Twelve to eighteen month olds watched a word video for four weeks and learned no more words than babies without it.

beats.text: The most learning came from parents teaching the words in everyday routines.
beats.say: The most learning came from parents teaching the words in everyday routines.

beats.text: Parents who liked the DVD thought it taught more than it did.
beats.say: Parents who liked the video thought it taught more than it did.

beats.text: A second trial: 12 to 15 months, 6 weeks of a word DVD.
beats.say: A six week trial with twelve to fifteen month olds found the same.

beats.text: Across 59 reports, children learned less from video than from a live person.
beats.sub: Ages 0 to 6. The gap shrank as children grew.
beats.say: Across fifty nine reports, children learned less from video than from a live person.

beats.text: The honest catch: these trials tested only word videos and word learning.
beats.sub: Not every kind of screen use. And the review's authors say some studies may overstate the gap.
beats.say: The honest catch is that these trials only tested word videos, and the review's authors say some studies may overstate the gap.

beats.text: Name the cup in the bath, the spoon at dinner, the sock while dressing.
beats.sub: Then wait for your baby's turn.
beats.say: Tonight, name the cup in the bath, the spoon at dinner, the sock while dressing, then wait.
